styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Old town, cathedral and the City of Arts and Sciences.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Paella, tapas bars and the Central Market.

styles.label: Beach
styles.blurb: City beach, promenade walks and long summer evenings.

stays.why: Walk to the cathedral, Central Market and Plaza de la Virgen. Busiest and noisiest at night.
Old quarter with street art and small bars. Lively and central, but can be loud late.
Best food and café scene; flat 15–20 minute walk to the old town.
Quieter, wide streets, good value; walkable to the centre and near the Turia park.

food: Try paella at lunch, not dinner. Valencians eat it midday; book a table at a proper restaurant.
Central Market (Mercat Central) is the place for jamón, olives and fresh produce. Go in the morning; check opening hours on the day.
Tapas and raciones in Ruzafa and El Carmen. Expect small plates to share, roughly €3–8 each.
Horchata with fartons is the local sweet drink. Try it at a horchatería in the afternoon.
The city water is fine to drink. Many bars charge for bread or a terrace seat; ask first.
more_time: Swap a beach afternoon for the Albufera lagoon south of the city: rice fields, boat trips and paella country. Check transport and tour options on the day.
Take a regional train from Estació del Nord to a nearby town for a half day. Buy tickets at the station.
Add a day for the City of Arts and Sciences: the science museum and oceanarium need several hours each.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the old town, the City of Arts and Sciences and a beach afternoon; add a night for the Albufera and a slower food day.

month_notes: January: cool, highs near 16°C and only about 3 rain days. Pack a warm layer.
February: still cool, highs around 17°C, a few more rain days. Good for museums.
March: mild at 19°C but the wettest month, about 8 rain days. Keep an indoor plan.
April: pleasant 20°C days, some rain. Great for walking the old town.
May: warm at 24°C with few rain days. Beach season starts.
June: hot at 28°C, dry. Use mornings and evenings for sightseeing.
July: hot, 31°C highs and 22°C nights, almost no rain. Beach and shade.
August: as hot as July, humid nights. Book air-conditioned rooms.
September: still warm at 27°C but rain returns, about 8 rain days.
October: comfortable 24°C days, some rain. Good all-round month.
November: cooler at 20°C, about 6 rain days. Quieter and cheaper.
December: cool at 17°C, few rain days. Bring a jacket for evenings.

climate_guide.summary: Mediterranean climate: mild winters, hot dry summers and a short rainy spell in spring and autumn.

items.title: Best time: May to June and September to October
items.text: Warm days around 24–28°C with few rain days. Good for both sightseeing and the beach.

items.title: July and August are hot
items.text: Highs of 31°C and nights near 22°C. Sightsee early, rest at midday, swim in the evening.

items.title: Rain peaks in March and September
items.text: About 8 rain days each. Showers are often short; carry a light rain jacket.

items.title: Mild winters
items.text: January and December highs of 16–17°C with cool nights near 7–8°C. A coat is enough.

items.title: Beach season
items.text: Sea and sand are best from June to September. May and October are fine for a walk, cooler for swimming.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light clothes and sunscreen for summer, a warm layer for winter, and a small umbrella in spring and autumn.

transit.best: Walk the flat centre; use metro or bus for the beach and the City of Arts and Sciences.

modes.text: Metro València has 9 lines, some trams. Single zone fare about €1.50 plus €1 for the card.
EMT buses reach most districts. Single ticket about €2, pay the driver by cash or card.
Taxis are metered; airport trips add a supplement. Uber, Bolt and Cabify operate.
Not needed in the city. Useful only for trips out to the Albufera or nearby towns.
The centre is flat and walkable. Bikes and the Turia park paths are popular.
Regional trains leave from Estació del Nord. No ferry service for visitors.
